subject: ENG
course_description: Readings in The Canterbury Tales, Troilus and Criseyde, and selected other works.
course_notes: Geoffrey Chaucer is one of the few English poets who has never not been read. We will read the full range of his poetry: dream visions, Troilus and Criseyde, and selected Canterbury Tales. Chaucer creates in English the stories and forms found in classical (e.g. Ovid's Metamorphoses and Virgil¿s Aeneid), vernacular (e.g. those by Dante, Boccaccio, and Guillaume de Lorris) and biblical traditions. Chaucer is at his best when overturning the conventions of epic, romance, fabliau, Breton lay, saint's life, and exemplum. We shall explore at least three of the great mysteries of Chaucer¿s life and work: how such a prolific poet could also be a soldier, diplomat, and court official; how his poetic persona consistently veils and deprecates his genius; and how his relationships with people from different social classes and sexes finds poetic expression. A class project will involve work with manuscript facsimiles in Emory¿s Rose Library. This course fulfills the pre-1700 requirement for the English major. Texts: The following Norton Critical Editions: Troilus and Criseyde, ed. Barney; The Canterbury Tales, ed. Kolve & Olson; Dream Visions and Other Poems, ed. Lynch.
